frontier.hypothesis: The 640 constant gets a block-head li and its own hard register when ALL of its uses lie inside one uninterrupted run of stores through the primitive pointer - i.e. the may-alias-pinned lw of D_800A374C (and the move $a1,$s0 that follows it) is what splits our store run and lets sched1 sink the 640 set.
frontier.mechanism: Matched sibling func_80072BC4's else-arm has three block-head constants with late first uses and no interruption in its store run; ours is the same shape except that the OT-base load sits between the RGB block and the two 640 uses. If the uninterrupted run is the discriminator, moving the OT-base computation so it no longer splits the run (while still emitting the lui/lw at target's position, which s1 proved is source-position-pinned) should let the 640 set stay at the block head with both stores late - the exact combination the s3 register-pin diagnostic proved is sufficient.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep chassis B with the ot local computed at each of: before the two 240 stores, immediately after them, between RGB subgroups, and after ALL coordinate stores (inline in the ot_Link call). For each, screen with tmp/grind/func_8003553C/s4/score.sh (~1.5 s/form) and record BOTH the difflines and whether the li 640 reaches the block head. This is cheap enough to also cross it with the two 640-store positions. Do NOT re-try the OT-base SPELLING variants (array-indexed slot, s32-staged base) - s3 measured those dead; this probe varies the load's POSITION relative to the store run, which is a different axis.

frontier.hypothesis: Reading the C of several more census hits whose block-head constant has the LARGEST gap to first use will expose the dataflow property (not syntax) that keeps GCC 2.7.2 from sinking a constant set.
frontier.mechanism: tmp/grind/func_8003553C/s4/census.py already produced 164 matched-function instances of exactly the codegen shape this function needs, ranked by gap. Each one's C source is direct evidence of a spelling whose constant survives sched1's sink; s4 only read the single closest hit. Reading the top ~6 and abstracting what their constants have in common turns guessing into reading.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run census.py (it prints func / index / gap / set / first-use), then for the top hits with gap >= 12 - func_80049E4C (gap 18, two instances), DispSamnailWindow (gap 16), func_80046048 (gap 16), func_80046B44 (gap 13/12), tslLineG5Init (gap 13) - Grep src/*.c for the function name and Read ONLY the function body with offset/limit. Tabulate: number of uses, whether the uses are interrupted by a call/load, whether the constant is a literal or a named local, and whether the stores are through a pointer or a global. Then transplant the common property, not the syntax.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual's remaining degree of freedom is the li's own slot among the three constants, and that sub-problem is separable from the store's slot.
frontier.mechanism: The s3 register-pin diagnostic (never committable) showed that with 640 in $3 every STORE lands in target's slot and the ONLY residual left is li 640 emitted after li 128 instead of ahead of li 240. So even a lever that wins the register may leave one instruction; conversely a lever that fixes the li order may be what wins the register (target materialises 640 FIRST, ahead of 240, despite 640's uses being LAST - which no form we have produced does).
frontier.next_probe: Treat 'get li 640 emitted ahead of li 240 while both 640 stores stay in the post-load group' as the primary objective rather than the store position, and screen forms on that criterion with score.sh plus a grep of the emitted asm, not on difflines alone. A form can be worth keeping even at difflines > 2 if it is the first one to put li 640 first with late stores, because the s3 diagnostic says the rest then follows.
